subject: Model catalog: provenance endorsements, timestamping, and pinning procedures
content:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: procurement@globex.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Model catalog RFI — provenance endorsements, timestamping, attachments included

Hi Sara and team,

Attached is our initial RFI response pack focusing on model catalog provenance, licensing endorsements, and pinning procedures (Globex_RFI_Model_Catalog_Responses_v1.pdf). High-level notes below — we pulled these into the attached as well.

- Provenance model: every model in the Redwood catalog includes a manifest that records source repository commit, licensing statement, training data provenance summary (where applicable), and a unique model artifact hash (SHA-256).
- Endorsements: for curated vendor models we include vendor-supplied attestations. For open models we include upstream license text, required attribution, and our recommended usage mappings.
- Timestamping: artifacts are timestamped at build/ingest time. We can provide a signed manifest (SHA-256 + Redwood signature) and optionally sign manifests using your KMS if you provide a signing key.
- Pinning & updates: customers can pin to a specific model version (artifact hash). We support automatic rollout policies (canary, staged) and offer rollback to any pinned artifact for 180 days by default.

Please see the SBOM export (sbom_export_20261103.txt) for an example manifest and the matrix describing pinning semantics (model-pinning-matrix.xlsx).

Next steps: can you confirm the specific deliverables you need for procurement vs. legal (signed attestation, sample manifest, or DocuSign-ready language)? Happy to set up a short tech deep-dive.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0143

From: Sara Choi <procurement@globex.com>

Subject: Re: Model catalog RFI — provenance endorsements, timestamping, attachments included

Monica,

Thanks for the quick turn. A few clarifying items from procurement and legal so we can include the right artifacts in our vendor packet: 

1) When you say "signed manifest," do you mean an internal Redwood PKI signature, or can you generate a time-stamped manifest signed with our customer KMS/HSM? We need the latter for our audit trail.
2) For timestamping, do you integrate with a third-party time-stamp authority (TSA) or provide an RFC-compliant time-stamp token?
3) For model pinning, please confirm SLA around freeze/unfreeze operations and whether rollback is a manual or automated operation. Also include any limits on retention of pinned artifacts.
4) Will the SBOM include attribution/license text for all third-party components (including tokenizer/token libraries)?

Legal specifically asked for sample language for a short attestation we can place in our contract — are you able to provide a DocuSign-ready attestation statement?

If you can reply with the brief answers above plus a proposed timeline for any signed artifacts, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Sara Choi
Senior Procurement Manager
Globex Corporation
procurement@globex.com

On Wed, Nov 4, 2026 at 10:05 AM Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
To: procurement@globex.com, monica_patel@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Model catalog RFI — provenance endorsements, timestamping, attachments included

Hi Sara (and team),

Thanks for the clear questions — below are concise answers and the practical steps we propose.

1) Signing & customer KMS: we support both. By default our ingestion pipeline signs manifests using Redwood's signing key and stores the signed manifest in the catalog. For customers who require customer-key signing, we can integrate with your KMS/HSM via an onboarding connector: you provide a signing key (or we call your signing service via a customer-managed endpoint) and we produce manifests signed with your key.

2) Timestamping and TSA: we produce RFC 3161-compatible time-stamp tokens on request. Our standard process records a server-side timestamp (ISO 8601) and we can submit a time-stamp token from a trusted TSA for high-assurance audits. We attach the token to the manifest (see sbom_export_20261103.txt for example fields: model_hash, build_commit, ingest_timestamp, tsa_token).

3) Pinning SLA & lifecycle: freeze/unfreeze operations are API-driven. We offer two modes: 
   - Immediate pin (sync): takes effect within 5s and is reversible; metadata retained for 180 days.
   - Managed rollouts: canary/staged deployments across Dedicated pools; rollbacks are supported and can be automated based on configured health checks.
Retention policy: pinned artifact metadata and manifests retained 540 days by default; full artifact retention is configurable per contract.

4) SBOM and license attribution: SBOM includes declared licenses for model code and third-party libraries we ship; for training data provenance we provide a summary and upstream license references where available. Tokenizers, runtimes, and common libraries are included in the export.

5) DocuSign-ready attestation: we maintain a short attestation template. Example clause we can populate and deliver via DocuSign: 
   "Redwood Inference attests that the model artifact identified by SHA-256 <model_hash> was ingested on <date> and the attached manifest accurately reflects the recorded provenance and license information. Redwood will, upon request and subject to the customer's onboarding, sign manifest artifacts with the customer's designated signing key or provide TSA-backed time-stamp tokens."

Attachments: model-pinning-matrix.xlsx (pinning semantics and API examples) and sbom_export_20261103.txt (sample manifest + TSA token example).

Proposed timeline: 1–3 business days to produce a customer-signed manifest (assuming KMS connectivity), 2–4 days to provide a DocuSign-ready attestation after legal sign-off.

If helpful we can also run a short screen-share to show the audit logs and the vault-based signing flow.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Product — Model Governance
Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwoodinference.com
